body:
Can you describe more about the fix, I feel like I am running into the same problem with qwen3.6. I am serving the model fine and can hit it over the openai endpoints, but Hermes seems to be running into several problems:

1. The agent itself isn't even recognizing all the tools it has available from /tools list 
2. It can't call tools.

This isn't just qwen either, I also hooked it up to opus and am hitting the same problem so it feels more like a general incompatibility with Spark?

<!-- hermes-sweeper:item=38376 -->
<!-- hermes-sweeper:verdict=close reason=not_planned confidence=high -->
Thanks for the detailed diagnosis. This is an automated hermes-sweeper review.

- Hermes deliberately dispatches only structured `tool_calls` (`agent/conversation_loop.py:4447`); converting `<|tool_call>…` text into executable calls would add a new model-output reconstruction path.
- This falls under the standing `model-output-repair` policy: Hermes does not repair or infer malformed/noncompliant model tool output.
- Hermes already has a display-only cleanup for several XML-shaped leaked tool-call blocks (`agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py:617`; commit `c345ec9a6384420805c862cbbf8363ed72b27a91`), but that intentionally does not execute text as a tool call.

Please configure the vLLM model/chat template and tool-call parser so its OpenAI-compatible response populates the structured `tool_calls` field. The later Qwen/Opus/Spark report is broader and lacks a reproducible configuration, so it does not establish a Gemma-specific adapter requirement.

---
*Closed as not-planned per standing maintainer policy (`model-output-repair`). This is a design-direction decision, not a code-quality judgment — see the Contribution Rubric in `AGENTS.md` for what the project is looking for. If you believe this policy was misapplied to your change, comment here and a maintainer will take a look.*
